channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nicotine vapes best chance to quit smoking, major review finds
item.description: Nicotine vapes being described as one of the best chances to quit smoking should shift the tone of the debate. Adult smokers need clear advice about options that can move them away from combustible tobacco, not messaging that makes every nicotine product sound equally dangerous. Vaping is not risk-free, but its value lies in comparison with continued smoking. Public health communication should make that hierarchy understandable enough for people to use it. (Published on August 26, 2026bybbc.com)

item.title: Anti-vaping hysteria keeps smokers hooked. Trump’s FDA is (finally) embracing reality
item.description: FDA authorisation of lower-risk nicotine products matters because it gives smokers something more useful than fear. A credible harm reduction framework should recognise products that can reduce exposure to combustion while maintaining strong standards for evidence, marketing and youth protection. The aim is not to normalise nicotine use, but to make the path away from cigarettes more realistic for adults who still smoke. Regulation should reward products that can help reduce harm, not keep the most dangerous option as the easiest one to find. (Published on August 26, 2026bywashingtonexaminer.com)

item.title: Canada Cut Tobacco Taxes and Crushed the Black Market
item.description: Canada’s tobacco tax cut shows that illicit markets are not untouchable. Price matters, and extreme excise can stop working as public health policy once illegal cigarettes become the cheaper, easier option. Reducing the black market does not mean giving up on lower smoking rates; it means designing incentives that keep consumers inside legal, accountable channels. A serious strategy should combine realistic taxation, enforcement and access to safer nicotine alternatives. (Published on August 26, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Dutch online cigarette and vape ban fails to stop young adults buying through social media
item.description: The Dutch online sales ban shows the limit of policies that remove legal access without removing demand. Young adults are still finding cigarettes and vapes through social media, where age checks, product standards and accountability are far weaker. That is not effective control; it is displacement into channels regulators can barely oversee. A better approach would focus on enforceable safeguards, responsible retailing and a legal market that is easier to monitor than the illegal one. (Published on August 26, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Smoking Harm Warning Labels: Why They Mislead
item.description: Smoking harm warning labels should tell the truth clearly enough to change behaviour. The greatest danger comes from burning tobacco, yet many warnings still fail to explain the difference between combustible cigarettes and lower-risk nicotine alternatives. That gap matters because smokers may understand that smoking is harmful without knowing there are less dangerous ways to move away from it. Better risk communication should warn, inform and guide people towards choices that reduce harm. (Published on August 26, 2026bytobaccoharmreduction.net)
